beats.label: S1 · The Massacre
beats.text: On Saint Brice's Day, King Æthelred orders every Dane in England slaughtered; King Canute answers by mustering a revenge army at Kattegat.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the whole season and the invasion of England in motion.

beats.label: S1 · Last Daughter of Uppsala
beats.text: Greenlanders Leif and Freydís reach Kattegat; Freydís kills the Christian who raped her, and Jarl Haakon soon names her the Last Daughter of Uppsala.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Freydís as a pagan icon — the identity every future season is built around.

beats.label: S1 · Bridge Falls
beats.text: Leif and Harald sabotage London Bridge, collapsing it under Edmund's forces; Canute crowns himself the first Viking King of England.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Binds Leif and Harald as brothers-in-arms and puts Canute on England's throne.

beats.label: S1 · Emma and Godwin
beats.text: Canute marries Queen Emma and elevates her advisor Godwin to earl of Wessex; Godwin secretly stabs King Edmund to seal Canute's throne.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the London power triangle — Canute, Emma, Godwin — that drives every later English plot.

beats.label: S1 · Kåre's Crusade
beats.text: The zealot Jarl Kåre massacres pagan Uppsala and allies with Olaf, Harald's Christian half-brother, to purge Norway's pagans and seize Kattegat.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Kattegat is invaded and why Freydís will spend future seasons defending pagans.

beats.label: S1 · Battle for Kattegat
beats.text: Kåre's zealots storm Kattegat's walls; Jarl Haakon falls and Freydís beheads Kåre, but Olaf then attacks in turn, killing Liv in Leif's arms.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The death of Liv is what breaks Leif and pushes him onto every later road he walks.

beats.label: S1 · Forkbeard's Fleet
beats.text: Forkbeard arrives with Canute's fleet and Olaf's men abandon him; Harald and Freydís flee wounded, and Leif is found bloodied over Kåre's dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the three leads on the run and hands Denmark's crown-in-waiting a footing in Norway.

cliffhanger.text: Kattegat stands, but only barely. Olaf's coup collapsed when Forkbeard's fleet arrived; Harald and Freydís are wounded fugitives, and Leif is unrecognisable in his grief for Liv.
questions: Where can Freydís and the wounded Harald find refuge from the men still hunting them?
Will Leif turn his rage on Olaf, the man who killed Liv?
How long can Canute hold England when Emma and Godwin now share his court?

characters.name: Leif Erikson
characters.line: Greenlander sailor whose lover Liv was killed in Olaf's attack on Kattegat; now consumed by grief and rage.

characters.name: Freydís Eiríksdóttir
characters.line: Leif's sister, a shieldmaiden hailed as the Last Daughter of Uppsala, on the run wounded beside Harald.

characters.name: Harald Sigurdsson
characters.line: Norwegian prince and rightful heir to Norway, wounded and fleeing after his half-brother's coup.

characters.name: Jarl Olaf Haraldsson
characters.line: Harald's Christian half-brother; attacked Kattegat and killed Liv but was routed when Forkbeard's fleet arrived.

characters.name: King Canute
characters.line: Ruler of Denmark and now the first Viking King of England, newly married to Queen Emma.

characters.name: Queen Emma of Normandy
characters.line: Æthelred's widow, now Canute's queen and co-ruler of England in London.

characters.name: Godwin
characters.line: Ambitious English advisor whom Canute made earl of Wessex; secretly murdered King Edmund to keep the throne.

characters.name: King Forkbeard
characters.line: Canute's father, ruling in his absence; his fleet has just saved Kattegat from Olaf.

characters.name: Queen Ælfgifu
characters.line: Canute's Mercian first wife and mother of his elder sons, hungry for their claim on Norway and England.

beats.label: S2 · Olaf's Bargain
beats.text: Forkbeard captures the defeated Olaf; to save his son Magnus, Olaf swears to serve as advisor to Svein, Canute's boy crowned as new King of Norway.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Olaf, Magnus and Svein inside Kattegat's power structure — the pieces every later Norway plot moves.

beats.label: S2 · Sanctuary at Jomsborg
beats.text: Fleeing Olaf's bounty, Freydís reaches Jomsborg, where Lord Hárekr welcomes her as gyðja of a promised new Uppsala for hunted pagans.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Founds Freydís's stronghold and her role as pagan leader for every season that follows.

beats.label: S2 · The Dnieper
beats.text: Leif and Harald travel to Novgorod seeking an army; denied, they take Vitomir's silver south with a hired crew, bound for Constantinople.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sends Harald and Leif east — the road that leads them to the Byzantine court next season.

beats.label: S2 · Godwin's Ambition
beats.text: In London, Emma survives an assassin and tortures her lady Ælfwynn to death, uncovering that Godwin dreams of putting his own bloodline on England's throne.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names Godwin's real project — a dynasty of his own — and cracks his alliance with Emma.

beats.label: S2 · Hárekr's Betrayal
beats.text: Freydís bears Harald's son; Hárekr seizes the boy and orders her killed, but the Jomsvikings turn on him and stone him, restoring Freydís as their leader.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Delivers the son who anchors Freydís's future and confirms she rules Jomsborg outright.

beats.label: S2 · Olaf Falls
beats.text: Jorundr, exiled and rescued by Olaf, reveals Jomsborg's location; Freydís lures Olaf's fleet ashore, burns his army alive, and spears Olaf herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills Olaf and leaves Magnus alone as heir to that grievance — the engine of season three's Norway plot.

beats.label: S2 · Constantinople
beats.text: Godwin marries Canute's niece Gytha, seating his heirs beside Emma's; Harald and Leif reach Constantinople and learn Eleana is the Emperor's betrothed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Places Godwin's line inside the succession and hands Harald a court — and a woman — that shape season three.

cliffhanger.text: Freydís rules Jomsborg alone with a newborn and a fragile peace with Ælfgifu; Harald and Leif have arrived in a foreign capital where the woman Harald loves belongs to the Emperor; Emma has quietly warned Godwin she knows what he is.
questions: Can Freydís's peace with Ælfgifu hold, or will Norway's new rulers turn on Jomsborg?
What happens when Harald's love for Eleana collides with her betrothal to Emperor Romanos?
How far will Godwin's ambitions carry his and Gytha's children toward the English throne?

characters.name: Freydís Eiríksdóttir
characters.line: Gyðja and ruler of Jomsborg, mother to Harald's infant son, having killed Olaf and bought peace by returning Svein to Ælfgifu.

characters.name: Harald Sigurdsson
characters.line: Norwegian prince arrived in Constantinople with Emperor Romanos's favour, unaware Freydís has borne his child.

characters.name: Leif Erikson
characters.line: Constantinople-bound Greenlander mourning Mariam, drawn ever deeper into astrolabes, maps and knowledge.

characters.name: Emperor Romanos III
characters.line: Ruler of the Byzantine Empire, revealed at the end as the betrothed of Eleana, whom Harald has come to love.

characters.name: Queen Emma of Normandy
characters.line: Canute's queen in London, now certain Godwin ordered the attempt on her life and moving against him quietly.

characters.name: Godwin
characters.line: Earl of Wessex, newly married to Canute's niece Gytha and one royal death away from a claim on England.

characters.name: King Canute
characters.line: King of England and Denmark, absent from London warring with the Wends while Emma governs in his stead.

characters.name: Queen Ælfgifu
characters.line: Regent of Norway from Kattegat with her son Svein restored to her by Freydís's peace deal.

characters.name: Magnus Olafsson
characters.line: Olaf's surviving son, kept alive as Forkbeard's captive under the terms of his father's bargain.

beats.label: S3 · Syracuse
beats.text: Seven years on, Harald and Leif serve Byzantium; Leif's tunnel bomb cracks Syracuse, but General Maniakes uses the same powder to massacre its people.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Time-jumps the show, shows Leif's science turned into atrocity, and makes Maniakes his enemy.

beats.label: S3 · Magnus's Poison
beats.text: Olaf's son Magnus poisons Jomsborg's flour to kill Freydís; she outwits him, fakes her death, and leads her surviving people west toward Greenland.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Jomsborg and turns Freydís's story westward, toward Erik and the golden land.

beats.label: S3 · Zoe and Romanos
beats.text: Harald secretly loves Empress Zoe; Romanos, unable to father an heir, quietly encouraged the affair — until an assassin stabs him at a masked ball.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Harald's patron and puts him in a court where he is now a suspect, not a champion.

beats.label: S3 · Canute Dying
beats.text: Canute summons every son to Kattegat to name a successor as he dies; in Denmark, Harefoot and Godwin smother King Forkbeard in his bed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens the succession that decides who rules England — and shows how far Godwin will now go.

beats.label: S3 · Greenland Split
beats.text: Freydís reaches Greenland but her father Erik kills her captain and abducts her son Harald, refusing to let her sail west without him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Erik from ally to jailer and traps young Harald in Greenland for whatever comes next.

beats.label: S3 · Hardrada Rises
beats.text: Harald escapes prison, kills Maniakes, and returns home to save a captured Freydís from Magnus; he imprisons Magnus and takes the name Harald Hardrada.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Delivers the sole king of Norway — and the show's whole title figure — in his final form.

beats.label: S3 · Westward
beats.text: Canute dies; Godwin crowns Harefoot instead of Emma's chosen Edward, while Leif and Freydís sail west from Kattegat toward the golden land in her visions.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reshapes England around a young king Emma is already working, and launches the voyage to a new world.

cliffhanger.text: Freydís and Leif sail into the western unknown for a land she has only seen in visions; Harald sits alone on Norway's throne longing for the son he has never met; in London, Emma quietly steers a boy king while Godwin nurses his losses.
questions: Will Leif and Freydís's voyage west actually reach the golden land she has seen?
Can Harald Hardrada hold Norway alone with Magnus imprisoned rather than dead?
How long before Emma's grip on Harefoot slips and Godwin turns on her?

characters.name: Freydís Eiríksdóttir
characters.line: Sailed west from Kattegat with Leif to find the golden land, leaving her young son behind in Greenland.

characters.name: Leif Erikson
characters.line: Navigator sailing westward with his sister, guided by Calinicus's map beyond the edge of every known chart.

characters.name: Harald Hardrada
characters.line: Sole king of Norway with Magnus in chains, still longing to one day meet the son he never knew he had.

characters.name: Queen Emma of Normandy
characters.line: Widowed dowager at court in London, quietly working the young Harefoot to keep her hand on England.

characters.name: King Harefoot
characters.line: Newly crowned King of England, having killed his own grandfather Forkbeard to reach the throne.

characters.name: Godwin
characters.line: Earl of Wessex whose gamble on Harefoot put a puppet on the throne but cost him Emma's trust.

characters.name: Magnus Olafsson
characters.line: Olaf's son, imprisoned by Harald after his coup in Norway collapsed but left alive as a hostage.

characters.name: Erik the Red
characters.line: Greenland patriarch who killed Freydís's captain and abducted her son to force her to stay.

characters.name: Harald (Freydís's son)
characters.line: Freydís and Harald's young boy, raised among the Kalaallit in Greenland and now under the healer Stígr's protection.
